newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Investors interested in Czech Poldi steel - minister.
newsitem.headline: Investors interested in Czech Poldi steel - minister.

text.p: Close to 10 Czech and foreign investors have shown an interest in taking over the troubled steelmill Poldi Ocel s.r.o., Industry and Trade Minister Vladimir Dlouhy said on Friday.
But Dlouhy, speaking at a news conference, warned that no progress could be made in Poldi's restructuring under its current ownership.
Dlouhy said that the mill, whose production has been interrupted for months due to a lack of financing, will collapse if its current owners do not reach a deal with the state on its future.

Poldi's majority owner, Bohemia Art s.r.o., has failed to pay up for part of the 54.8 percent stake it bought from the government privatisation agency, the National Property Fund (NPF), and the state is now negotiating with the firm on a settlement.
Bohemia Art owners, Vladimir Stehlik and Marko Stehlik, are facing a criminal investigation and have been charged with abuse of commercial information.
The state has called on the Stehliks to leave the firm, but they demand compensation.
"According to my information... the talks are unfortunately not leading to the desired conclusion," Dlouhy said.
He did not name the potential investors, but confirmed earlier reports in the local press that Czech steel maker Trinecke Zelezarny a.s. was one of them.
The minister told reporters that the state might help Poldi out after Bohemia Art leaves and a new investor is found.
